edits.old: MongoDB's streaming-write guide maps Trigger.Continuous(...) to continuous processing and says other or omitted triggers use micro-batches. Apache Spark's current Structured Streaming page describes Real-Time Mode with Trigger.RealTime, requires update output mode, and limits supported sinks. These pages do not establish that MongoDB's documented continuous-write path is equivalent to Spark Real-Time Mode or that the MongoDB sink is supported there; treat compatibility as unresolved for the selected versions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
edits.new: MongoDB's streaming-write guide maps Trigger.Continuous(<time value>) to continuous processing and says any other Trigger, or no trigger call, uses micro-batch processing. Apache Spark's Real-time Mode page describes Trigger.RealTime, requires the update output mode, and allows only Kafka, foreach, console and memory sinks (other sinks fail with SINK_NOT_SUPPORTED). That sink list does not include a MongoDB sink, and the MongoDB guide does not mention Real-time Mode, so MongoDB's continuous-write path (Trigger.Continuous) should not be assumed equivalent to Spark Real-time Mode, and the MongoDB sink is not among Spark's listed supported sinks. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/spark-connector/current/streaming-mode/streaming-write.md ; https://apache.github.io/spark/streaming/real-time-mode.html

evidence.quote: To use continuous processing, pass `Trigger.Continuous(<time value>)` as an argument, where `<time value>` is how often you want the Spark Connector to asynchronously checkpoint.
If you pass any other static method of the `Trigger` class, or if you don't call `writeStream.trigger()`, the Spark connector uses micro-batch processing instead.
The output mode must be update. Any other output mode fails to start with
Other sinks fail with STREAMING_REAL_TIME_MODE.SINK_NOT_SUPPORTED.
Console and memory sinks, which are useful for development and debugging.

statements.note: Two distinct settings with these roles; the 'which rows' wording is an accurate paraphrase of Spark's output-mode description.

edits.rationale: Spark's outputMode specifies what gets written to the sink, while the connector's operationType specifies the type of write operation (insert, replace, update). The streaming write configuration page lists the stated defaults: replace, _id and true. The defaults are on the config page, not the streaming-write page originally cited.
